neighbours.label: comparative degree constructions: 'more'/'less' plus an adjective or adverb (the - pole peaks on ' more' x20, ' Greater', Arabic 'اكثر', and fires on the comparative adjective; bare positive-degree adjectives score ~0)
fire: The electric van is more economical than the petrol one.
She answered more confidently than the other candidate.
The coastal town is more crowded in July.
The revised edition is more accurate than the first.
He drives more carefully than his sister.
The attic room is more spacious than it looks.
The new plan is less ambitious but safer.
The nights feel more peaceful than the days.
quiet: The coastal town is crowded in July.

notes: Card: ' more' dominates the top 32 (x20) plus Greater/اكثر. Probes: 'more/less + adjective' sentences fire 0.17-0.48 (peaking on the adjective or on ' more'); the same sentences with the bare adjective score <= 0.005; 'less'/'fewer' sentences also fire, so the trigger is the comparative degree word, not 'more' alone.
